subject: pixelDungeonProps
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: dungeon props: chest, torches, barrels, bones, spike trap.
Style: pixel art.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact dungeon prop module in pixel art style, using the pixel kit utilities for texture and shading plus a glow kit for torch flames, built as a static model without joints since it doesn't need articulation.

I'm laying out the scene: a chest centered at the back, floor-standing torch braziers, barrels, a pile of bones, and a spiked trap plate, spread across the x-axis. I'm defining helper functions for boxes with tiled textures and planning pixel textures for wood planks, stone, metal, bone, and flame details with consistent seam shading and nail details.

Now I'm building the barrel geometry using a lathe profile for the curved staves, with cell-based paint for wood grain and darker iron hoops layered as rings around the barrel body.

Designing a generalized barrel function parameterized by center and axis so both upright and tipped barrels share the same lathe and hoop logic, just rotated along a different direction vector.

For the chest, I'm planning the base as a simple box and the curved lid as an extruded arch profile along the box's length, approximating a rounded top rather than a true half-cylinder.

Now I'm setting up a wood plank paint pattern with seams and brown color variation, then adding iron strap details—vertical bands across the lid and base with corner reinforcements.

I'm also adding a gold lock plate with keyhole texture, a few spilled gold coins in front of the closed chest, and designing standing torches with stone bases, iron poles, and crossed textured planes for the flame glow.

Mapping out exact positions now—chest centered, torches flanking at x=±1.15, and a barrel cluster on the left side spaced far enough apart (roughly 0.7 units) so their radii don't overlap.

Then I'm placing a tipped barrel to the side and designing a spike trap platform on the right at x=1.9: a stone plate with a 4x4 grid of pits, cone-shaped iron spikes rising from some holes, and a few bloodstained tips for grim detail.

Now I'm adding a bone pile in front: a skull built from a box cranium with a textured face plane for eye sockets, a separate jaw box with small teeth, plus rib and femur bones made from boxes with knob ends at the joints.

Still defining rib curves... Now for bone coloring I'll use a tan-to-cream ramp shaded by surface normal. For the spike trap, I'm adding a pressure plate texture with a flagstone pattern and maybe a faint rune carving in the center.

For the stone tiles I'm generating a pixel texture with brick rows in varying greys, and pits for the spikes will just be dark boxes sunk slightly above the trap's top surface so the spikes appear to rise from holes. Lighting-wise I'm giving the torches and flames a glow while keeping things like coins and the chest lock plain, skipping extras like lanterns or rats, and the part count is settling around 150.

I'm keeping the flat color palette tight, under twenty distinct colors for iron, dark stone, gold, and ember tones, and I'm setting up the import structure and builder config before writing the dungeon props model, planning to use direction-based rotation rather than bones since these are static parts.

Writing helper functions...

Still writing wood paint logic...

Now I'm sketching a barrel-building function that computes an axis vector based on whether the barrel is tipped over, finds its center point, and lathes a stave profile along that axis with the right segment count and color.

I'm adding hoop rings around the barrel using cylinder geometry, matching radius and position to the lathe profile at a few heights, and slightly bumping the radius so the hoops clear the lathe's vertex geometry without mismatched orientation.

I'm also handling the lid: for an open barrel I'm placing a dark water disc near the top, otherwise a circular plank-textured disc at both the top and bottom ends, oriented along the barrel's axis with the plank texture mapped across the whole disc.

Now I'm moving on to the torch structure, building it from a stone base and socket, an iron pole, a few wrapped iron bands along its length, and starting on a lathe-based cup at the top.

Adding the charred top, ember glow, and flame cards, then sketching the pixel-art flame pattern row by row...

Still writing pixel pattern rows...

With the grid finalized, I'm defining the color palette for the card sprites and setting up a frame-based card layout system with glow effects applied to the meshes.

Now I'm building the treasure chest geometry: a wood-paint base box, a darker trim rim along the bottom, and an arched lid outline defined as a set of 2D points to extrude.

Writing lid straps...

Then I'm adding base straps as boxes positioned on either side, plus small corner brackets for an iron band look, and a front gold lock plate with a pixel-art keyhole design on top.

Adding more scene details...

Adding a warning rune and finishing the spike trap, I'm moving on to a bones pile with a skull and ribs, using a rotation helper to position parts consistently under a yaw transform.

Lower jaw settles near the floor at y .02-.06, leaving a slight gap-open look. Rather than modeling individual teeth, I'll add face details via textured planes: a cranium-front plane with eye sockets and nose, plus a maxilla-front plane with a simple teeth texture, oriented with proper yaw rotation to face forward.

Designing the pixel texture for the skull face...

Positioning the teeth plane near the maxilla, then moving on to the femur bones—using helper rod functions with box-shaped cross-sections and small cube knobs at each end to suggest joint bulges.

I'm adjusting the skull position to rest raised above the crossed femurs, lifting its base by .09 so the jaw clears the bone tops, then placing a separate ribcage cluster near the chest front-left area.

Now I'm laying out the ribcage with a spine rod and six curved ribs per side, using bezier arcs that rise up and out before settling back down to look like collapsed bones, tapering their thickness along the length.

I'm deciding to add a few scattered loose bone fragments nearby but skip extras like vertebrae detail, pelvis, or a rat, keeping the sweep caps flat with a boxy bone-colored section. I'm also skipping cobwebs and shackles, and now working out where the torch's flame should sit on top of its mount.

Now I'm writing a procedural stone-tile texture generator that lays down a brick-like grid, darkens the mortar seams, and adds subtle highlight/shadow noise to each tile for a weathered stone look.

I'm also sketching a plank texture for barrel lids with horizontal seams and streaky grain, separate from the main wood paint used elsewhere, before moving on to finalize the torch cup details.

Now I'm adding coins near the chest front using small cylinder geometry, stacking a few and scattering others flat with alternating gold and rim colors, plus tiny glowing spark boxes above each torch and an extra iron bracket ring on the pole. Then I'll finish writing out the full scene code and return the root object.

I'm defining the iron paint colors, a rod helper for connecting points with box-section geometry, and a hoop radius interpolation function along the barrel profile. For the skull pieces I'm working out a yaw rotation helper that rotates offset positions around the Y axis so parts align correctly.
